newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban release U.N. plane with Tajik rebel chief.
newsitem.headline: Taleban release U.N. plane with Tajik rebel chief.

text.p: The Taleban militia released a U.N. plane on Sunday that had been forced to land in western Afghanistan, apparently with a Tajik Islamic rebel leader on board, U.N. officials said.
They said the plane had left the Soviet-built military airbase of Shindand, about 120 km (75 miles) south of Herat, to complete its flight to Kunduz in northern Afghanistan.
Jets of the radical Islamic Taleban militia had forced the U.N.-chartered plane to land at Shindand on Saturday when on its way from the eastern Iranian city of Mashhad to Kunduz.
"We have released the plane and authorised it to fly because it is now clear that it is a U.N. plane," said a spokesman for the Taleban governor of Herat, Mullah Yar Mohammad.
"We respect the United Nations, but we request that we should be notified about any future U.N. flight," said the spokesman, contacted by telephone.

Iranian radio and sources in Pakistan said the plane, chartered by the United Nations in the Tajik capital Dushanbe, was carrying Tajik Islamic opposition leader Sayed Abdullo Nuri for a planned meeting with Tajik President Imamali Rakhmonov.
